I’ve been farming these 200 mu in Quzhou for 25 years, and my old man taught me the basics before that. I finished middle school, so I can read a fertilizer bag and do the sums, but at the end of the day I trust what I’ve seen with my own eyes and what the neighbors are doing. With 200 mu and just me and my wife, I hire the rotary tiller and the combine, but I stand there and watch them set the depth myself. I learned that lesson the hard way.

My main land is 160 mu in the wheat-maize double crop. That’s the bread and butter. The other 40 mu I split: 20 mu of autumn cabbage near the well where I can water it, and 20 mu of summer millet on the drier corner.

For the winter wheat on those 160 mu, I sow an improved variety—Jimai or something like it, whatever the seed shop has that my neighbors had good luck with last year. At sowing in October I put down 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, that’s one full 50 kg bag. Then at green-up I irrigate, and at jointing I top-dress with 15 kg of urea per mu. Some years I put another 5 kg urea at booting if the weather looks dry. I irrigate three times: winter water around New Year, jointing water in April, and grain filling in May. I spray twice—once for weeds right after sowing, and once in spring if I see rust or aphids. I use rotary tillage before sowing. Last year I got 550 kg per mu, and I expect the same this year if the spring rain cooperates.

For summer maize, as soon as the wheat comes off in June I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid. Everyone around here uses it, and it works. I no-till sow directly into the wheat stubble with the machine—saves diesel and time. I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu in the row at sowing, then at big trumpet stage I spread 20 kg urea per mu. Two irrigations: one at sowing if it hasn’t rained, and one at grain filling in August. Two sprays: herbicide right after sowing, and one for corn borer in July. I expect about 600 kg per mu.

The 20 mu of autumn cabbage I plant in August with hybrid F1 seed. Cabbage is greedy. I put down 50 kg compound per mu at transplanting, then side-dress twice with urea, about 15 kg each time, plus some potassium sulfate because the dealer said it helps the heads tighten. Four irrigations, three pesticide sprays for caterpillars and downy mildew. Rotary tillage to break up the soil fine. I expect 4,500 kg per mu if the market doesn’t crash.

The 20 mu of millet is an improved variety, planted in June. Millet doesn’t need babying. I put 30 kg compound per mu at sowing, and if it looks pale I top-dress 5 kg urea at heading. Two irrigations, one spray for armyworm. Rotary tillage before sowing. I expect 350 kg per mu.

I watch my costs. Fertilizer got expensive, so I think twice, but I’d rather put down a little too much than watch my yield drop. A bad year means I lose real money; an extra bag of urea is just a cost. I do what my neighbors do—if the whole village is putting 20 kg urea on corn, I do the same. You don’t stick your neck out when you’ve got 200 mu to pay for.
